"'''Billie Jean'''" is a song by the American singer [[Michael Jackson]], released by [[Epic Records]] on January 2, 1983, as the second single from Jackson's sixth studio album, ''[[Thriller (album)|Thriller]]'' (1982). It was written by Jackson and produced by Jackson and [[Quincy Jones]]. "Billie Jean" blends [[post-disco]], [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]], [[funk]] and [[dance-pop]]. The lyrics describe a young woman, Billie Jean, who claims that the narrator is the father of her newborn son, which he denies. Jackson said that the lyrics were based on [[groupie]]s' claims about Jackson's older brothers when Jackson toured with them as members of [[the Jackson 5]].

"Billie Jean" reached number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], topped the [[Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs|''Billboard'' Hot Black Singles]] chart within three weeks, and became Jackson's fastest-rising number one single since his time as a member of the Jackson 5. It reached number one in the UK, Australia, Canada, France, Ireland, Switzerland and Belgium, and the top ten of the music charts in many other countries. "Billie Jean" was one of the best-selling singles of 1983, helping ''Thriller'' become the [[List of best-selling albums|best-selling album of all time]], and became Jackson's best-selling solo single. "Billie Jean" is [[RIAA certification|certified diamond]] in the US and with 18 million copies worldwide, is one of the [[List of best-selling singles#Highest-certified singles|highest-selling singles of all time]]. In 2026, following the release of the biopic ''[[Michael (2026 film)|Michael]]'', "Billie Jean" surged on streaming platforms globally<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/en-ca/entertainment/music/michael-jackson-s-billie-jean-peaks-again-on-spotify-global-chart-43-years-after-release/ar-AA21JkRJ?gemSnapshotKey=GM698A82CF-snapshot-1&cvid=6a15ff5dbe2f431d94a080f66bb66e3a&ei=19|title=Michael Jackson’s 'Billie Jean' peaks again on Spotify global chart 43 years after release|publisher=Inde News |access-date=2026-05-15 }}</ref> and became Jackson's first number-one single on the [[Billboard Global 200|''Billboard'' Global 200]] chart.<ref name=global/>

Jackson's performance of "Billie Jean" on the TV special ''[[Motown 25: Yesterday, Today, Forever]]'' was nominated for an [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Individual Performance in a Variety or Music Program|Emmy Award]]. It introduced a number of Jackson's signatures, including the [[moonwalk (dance)|moonwalk]], rhinestone glove, black sequined jacket, and high-water pants, and was widely imitated. The "Billie Jean" [[music video]], which was directed by [[Steve Barron]], was the first performance by a black artist to be aired in heavy rotation on [[MTV]]. Along with the other videos produced for ''Thriller'', it helped establish MTV and make videos an integral part of [[popular music]] marketing. The spare, bass-driven arrangement helped pioneer what one critic called "sleek, post-soul pop music".<ref name="Blender"/>

"Billie Jean" received honors including two [[Grammy Award]]s and an [[American Music Awards|American Music Award]]. ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' ranked it as the No. 2 song for 1983. A list compiled by ''[[Rolling Stone]]'' and MTV in 2000 ranked "Billie Jean" the sixth-greatest pop song since 1963. ''Rolling Stone'' placed it at number 58 on its list of [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time]] in 2004, and at number 44 in its updated 2021 list. The song was also included in the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]]'s [[500 Songs that Shaped Rock and Roll]].<ref>{{cite web|title= Experience the Music: One Hit Wonders and the Songs that Shaped Rock and Roll |publisher= Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum |url= http://rockhall.com/exhibits/one-hit-wonders-songs-that-shaped-rock-and-roll/ |archive-date= May 9, 2012 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120509180015/http://rockhall.com/exhibits/one-hit-wonders-songs-that-shaped-rock-and-roll/}}</ref>

sections.wikitext:
[[File:Billie Jean music video.jpg|thumb|right|alt=A male is shown standing in a bent down position on his toes on top of an illuminated tile. He is wearing a black jacket and pants with white shoes and a pink shirt. Behind the male a grey narrow path can be seen as well as buildings in the far background.|Jackson landing on his toes and illuminating a tile in the music video for "Billie Jean"]]
[[MTV]] initially refused to air the video for "Billie Jean", as the network's executives felt [[African-American music|black music]] did not fit into its "[[Rock music|rock]]"-centered programming at the time.{{sfn|Campbell|1993|p=58}} Enraged by their refusal despite Jackson's success as a musical artist, [[Walter Yetnikoff]], the president of Jackson's record company [[CBS Records International|CBS Records]], threatened to expose MTV's stance on racial discrimination: "I said to MTV, 'I'm pulling everything we have off the air, all our product. I'm not going to give you any more videos. And I'm going to go public and fucking tell them about the fact you don't want to play music by a black guy.'"<ref name="Blender"/> MTV relented and premiered the "Billie Jean" music video on March 10, 1983.<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Tamara |last= Palmer |title= How the 'Billie Jean' Video Changed MTV |magazine= [[The Root (magazine)|The Root]] |date= March 10, 2013 |access-date= March 27, 2019 |url= https://www.theroot.com/how-the-billie-jean-video-changed-mtv-1790895543}}</ref> After the video was aired in [[heavy rotation]], ''Thriller'' went on to sell an additional 10 million copies.<ref name="Blender"/><ref>{{cite magazine|first= Jay |last= Cocks |title= Sing a Song of Seeing |magazine= [[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date= December 26, 1983 |access-date= February 15, 2009 |url= http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,926425-3,00.html |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090820032442/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,926425-3,00.html |archive-date= August 20, 2009}}</ref> It was one of the first videos by a black artist to be aired regularly by the channel.{{sfn|Campbell|1993|p=58}}

Directed by [[Steve Barron]] and produced by Gowers Fields Flattery, the video shows a photographer who follows but never catches Jackson, as when photographed Jackson fails to materialize on the developed picture. Jackson dances to Billie Jean's hotel room and as he walks along a sidewalk, each tile lights up at his touch.{{sfn|Campbell|1993|p=58}}<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Sean |last= Weitner |year= 2001 |title= Michael Jackson: A Life in Film |magazine= [[Flak Magazine]] |url= http://www.flakmag.com/music/mj/videos.html |archive-date= March 6, 2003 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20030306071527/http://www.flakmag.com/music/mj/videos.html}}</ref> After performing a quick spin, he jumps and lands, freeze framed, on his toes. Upon arrival at the hotel, he climbs the staircase to Billie Jean's room, lighting up each step as he touches it and illuminating a burnt-out "Hotel" sign as he passes it. The paparazzo then arrives at the scene and watches as Jackson vanishes under the covers of Billie Jean's bed, before the police arrive and arrest him for spying on Billie Jean.{{sfn|Campbell|1993|p=58}} As the paparazzo is led away, he drops a tiger-print cloth that Jackson had left behind after polishing his shoe with it earlier in the video. (On both occasions, the cloth briefly transforms into a tiger cub.) Once the street is empty, the paving tiles again light up in sequence, reversing Jackson's earlier progress.

Jackson's new look for the video, a black leather suit with a pink shirt and a red bow tie, was copied by children around the US.{{sfn|Campbell|1993|p=58}} Imitation became so severe that, despite pupil protests, [[Bound Brook High School]] forbade students from wearing a single white glove like Jackson had on during the performance of "Billie Jean" at ''[[Motown 25: Yesterday, Today, Forever]]''.<ref>{{cite news|title= School bans Michael Jackson attire |newspaper= [[Lakeland Ledger]] |date= March 13, 1984 |access-date= March 13, 2010 |url= https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=7NsvAAAAIBAJ&pg=6799,4585740&dq}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title= White gloves banned |newspaper= [[Ottawa Citizen]] |date= March 14, 1984 |access-date= March 13, 2010 |url= https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=jdEyAAAAIBAJ&pg=5326,1479180&dq}}</ref>

The short film was inducted into the Music Video Producers Hall of Fame in 1992.{{sfn|Halstead|2007|pp=38–40}} In a 2005 poll of 31 pop stars, video directors, agents, and journalists conducted by telecommunications company [[Hutchison 3G|3]], the music video was ranked fifth in their "Top 20 Music Videos Ever".<ref>{{cite news|first= David |last= Smith |newspaper= [[The Guardian]] |title= Cash tops Thriller with best video ever |date= January 30, 2005 |access-date= February 15, 2009 |url= https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2005/jan/30/arts.artsnews}}</ref> The video was also ranked as the 35th greatest music video in a list compiled by MTV and ''[[TV Guide]]'' at the millennium.{{sfn|Halstead|2007|pp=39–41}} On June 10, 2021, "Billie Jean" became the first 1980s clip by a solo artist to reach 1 billion views on [[YouTube]].<ref>{{cite news|first= Karu F. |last= Daniels |title= Michael Jackson's 'Billie Jean' music video hits 1 billion views on YouTube |newspaper= [[New York Daily News]] |date= June 17, 2021 |access-date= July 25, 2021 |url= https://www.nydailynews.com/snyde/ny-michael-jackson-billie-jean-video-youtube-one-billion-views-20210617-z37xpe5qb5bevbiany5osltko4-story.html}}</ref>

sections.wikitext: In 1984, [[Pepsi]] sponsored the [[The Jackson 5|Jacksons]]' [[Victory Tour (The Jacksons tour)|Victory Tour]]. In return, Michael and his brothers were to star in two commercials for the company.{{sfn|Taraborrelli|2004|pp=279–289}} Jackson had reworked "Billie Jean" for the commercial and titled it "Pepsi Generation". The song was used as the official [[jingle]] for the commercials and released as a 7-inch promo single. The launch of "The Choice of a New Generation" campaign in February 1984 was attended by 1,600 people who were issued with a programme and the 7-inch single.{{sfn|Halstead|2007|p=205}} During the filming of the second commercial, a firework in the rear of the set was prematurely detonated, setting Jackson's hair ablaze. The incident necessitated [[reconstructive surgery]].<ref>{{cite magazine|title= Milestones: Feb. 6, 1984 |magazine= [[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date= February 6, 1984 |access-date= February 15, 2009 |url= http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,954175,00.html |url-status= dead |archive-date= January 23, 2011 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110123032924/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,954175,00.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title= Singer Has Operation To Repair Burn Scar |newspaper= [[The New York Times]] |date= April 19, 1984 |access-date= February 15, 2009 |url= https://www.nytimes.com/1984/04/19/us/singer-has-operation-to-repair-burn-scar.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first= Richard |last= Zoglin |author-link= Richard Zoglin |title= Too Much Risk on the Set? |magazine= [[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date= February 13, 1984 |access-date= February 15, 2009 |url= http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,926474-1,00.html |url-status= dead |archive-date= October 11, 2011 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20111011123740/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,926474-1,00.html}}</ref> The commercials were premiered at the Grammy Awards, the same night he collected a record eight awards.{{sfn|Taraborrelli|2004|pp=279–289}}<ref>{{cite magazine|title= People: Mar. 12, 1984 |magazine= [[Time (magazine)|Time]] |date= March 12, 1984 |url= http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0%2C9171%2C921610%2C00.html |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20101106174828/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0%2C9171%2C921610%2C00.html |archive-date= November 6, 2010}}</ref>

Jackson's original version of "Billie Jean" was remixed by rapper [[Kanye West]] for ''[[Thriller 25]]'', a 25th anniversary reissue of Jackson's ''Thriller''. Titled "Billie Jean 2008", the remix garnered a mixed reception; most critics felt that it was impossible to improve upon the original. ''[[Pitchfork Media]]''{{'}}s Tom Ewing stated that the remix would have benefited from a guest verse by West, which "might have added dynamics to the mix's clumsy claustrophobia".<ref>{{cite web|first= Tom |last= Ewing |title= Michael Jackson – Thriller: 25th Anniversary Edition |website= [[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]] |date= February 15, 2008 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url= https://pitchfork.com/reviews/albums/11163-thriller-25th-anniversary-edition/}}</ref>

Mike Joseph, in a review of ''Thriller 25'' for ''[[PopMatters]]'', described the track listing of the reissue as "pleasant" but that West's "lazy" remix was the only exception. He added, "You've been given the opportunity to remix the most iconic single from one of the most iconic albums of all time, and all you can do is stick a drum machine on top of the song's original arrangement?".<ref>{{cite web|first= Mike |last= Joseph |title= Michael Jackson: Thriller 25 |work= [[PopMatters]] |date= February 10, 2008 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url= https://www.popmatters.com/pm/review/michael-jackson-thriller-25}}</ref> Rob Sheffield of ''Rolling Stone'' disliked the removal of the original bassline, and compared it to "putting [[Bobby Orr]] on the ice without a [[hockey stick]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|first= Rob |last= Sheffield |title= Michael Jackson – Thriller 25 Deluxe Edition |magazine= Rolling Stone |date= February 21, 2008 |url= https://www.rollingstone.com/reviews/album/18290476/review/18305830/thriller_25_deluxe_edition |archive-date= February 17, 2008 |url-status= dead |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080217033454/http://www.rollingstone.com/reviews/album/18290476/review/18305830/thriller_25_deluxe_edition}}</ref> [[IGN]]'s Todd Gilchrist praised West's remix and stated that it was a "pretty great track". He added, "it almost overplays the track's originally understated drama, his additions enhance the song and demonstrate that in a contemporary context."<ref>{{cite web|first= Todd |last= Gilchrist |title= Michael Jackson – Thriller 25th Anniversary Ed. |website= [[IGN]] |date= February 7, 2008 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url-status= dead |url= http://uk.music.ign.com/articles/850/850483p2.html |archive-date= June 30, 2009 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090630160309/http://uk.music.ign.com/articles/850/850483p2.html}}</ref>

"Billie Jean" aided ''Thriller'' in becoming the biggest selling album of all time. The song is recognized as one of the most cherished in history.<ref name="Guardian">{{cite news|title= How Billie Jean changed the world |newspaper= [[The Guardian]] |location= London |date= July 12, 2007 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url= https://www.theguardian.com/music/2007/jul/12/popandrock}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first= Ben |last= Rayner |title= The return of Michael Jackson's Thriller |newspaper= [[Toronto Star]] |date= February 10, 2008 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url= https://www.thestar.com/entertainment/article/302097}}</ref>

It was popularly believed that "Billie Jean" was an autobiographical song, referring to someone who claimed Jackson was the father of her child. Based on this theory, [[Lydia Murdock]] wrote the song "[[Superstar (Lydia Murdock song)|Superstar]]", which was a minor hit in 1983, intending this song as a criticism of Jackson's purported denial of paternity.<ref>{{cite book|first= John |last= Tobler |year= 1992 |title= NME Rock 'N' Roll Years |edition= 1st |publisher= [[Reed Elsevier|Reed International Books Ltd]] |location= London |page= 386 |id= CN 5585}}</ref> Another song referred to as an "answer song" was a rap song by [[T-Ski Valley]]. The song "[[Valley Style]]" was actually reviewed by [[James Hamilton (DJ and journalist)|James Hamilton]] in the 30 July issue of ''[[Record Mirror]]''. He referred to both Lydia Murdock's and T-Ski Valley's recordings as answer versions to "Billie Jean" but with a question mark for T-Ski Valley's rap version.<ref>''Record Mirror'', July 30, 1983 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/UK/Record-Mirror/80s/83/Record-Mirror-1983-07-30-OCR.pdf Page 28 Discos, from page 27, LYDIA MURDOCK:]</ref><ref>''Record Mirror'', July 30, 1983 - [https://www.worldradiohistory.com/UK/Record-Mirror/80s/83/Record-Mirror-1983-07-30-OCR.pdf Page 28 Discos, from page 27, T.SKI VALLEY:]</ref>

On his ''[[Late Night with David Letterman|Late Night]]'' program in the 1980s, host [[David Letterman]] often played a recording of a song with the word "chair" replacing "kid" to create the [[mondegreen]] "the chair is not my son".<ref name="chair">{{cite news|title= That song brings back memories: Billie Jean (the chair is not my son) |newspaper= [[WBEZ]] |location= Chicago, IL |date= June 26, 2009 |access-date= August 11, 2022 |url= https://www.wbez.org/stories/that-song-brings-back-memories-billie-jean-the-chair-is-not-my-son/7f7bb27b-400e-4b07-9cf3-4f3f0fd9bf83}}</ref>

Frequently listed in magazine polls of the best songs ever made, "Billie Jean" was named the greatest dance record of all time by [[BBC Radio 2]] listeners.<ref>{{cite news|title= Billie Jean voted top dance song |work= BBC News Online |date= July 15, 2008 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url= http://news.bbc.co.uk/nolpda/ifs_news/hi/newsid_7507000/7507218.stm}}{{dead link|date=September 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In a list compiled by ''Rolling Stone'' and MTV in 2000, the song was ranked as the sixth greatest pop song since 1963.<ref>{{cite news|title= Yesterday is top pop song |work= BBC News Online |date= November 17, 2000 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url= https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/1027940.stm}}</ref>

''Rolling Stone'' placed the song at number 58 on its list of [[Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time|The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time]] in 2004.<ref name="RS 2004">{{cite magazine|title= The RS 500 Greatest Songs of All Time (1-500) |magazine= [[Rolling Stone]] |url= http://www.rollingstone.com/news/coverstory/500songs/page/1 |url-status= dead |archive-date= October 23, 2006 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20061023195417/http://www.rollingstone.com/news/coverstory/500songs/page/1}}</ref> In the 2021 update of the list it had risen to 44.<ref name="RS 2021">{{cite magazine|title= The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time > Michael Jackson, 'Billie Jean' |magazine= [[Rolling Stone]] |date= September 15, 2021 |access-date= September 20, 2021 |url= https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-lists/best-songs-of-all-time-1224767/michael-jackson-billie-jean-4-1225294/}}</ref> "Billie Jean" was voted number 2 in ''[[The Nation's Favourite|The Nation's Favourite Number 1 Single]]'', a British TV program airing on [[ITV (TV network)|ITV]] on 21 July 2012. In a similar poll in 2015 the song was voted by the British public as the nation's second favorite [[List of UK Singles Chart number ones of the 1980s|1980s number one]].<ref>{{cite news|first= Caroline |last= Westbrook |title= The Nation's Favourite 80s Number One: 12 more classic 80s chart-toppers which didn't make the cut |newspaper= [[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]] |date= 25 July 2015 |access-date= 27 July 2015 |url= http://metro.co.uk/2015/07/25/the-nations-favourite-80s-number-one-12-more-classic-80s-chart-toppers-which-didnt-make-the-cut-5312786/}}</ref>

In an interview, [[Pharrell Williams]] stated that "Billie Jean" was one of his favorite songs. "It is hard to say if there is a greater song than 'Billie Jean'. I think there will never be a song like this one again, with this bassline, with this kind of effect, this eternalness, this perfection."{{sfn|Thriller 25: The Book|2008|p=26}} When re-released as part of the ''[[Visionary: The Video Singles|Visionary]]'' campaign in 2006, "Billie Jean" charted at No. 11 in the UK. It remained on the chart for over forty weeks and was the most successful reissue by a large margin.{{sfn|Halstead|2007|pp=39–41}} According to ''Thriller 25: The Book'' (2008), "Billie Jean" was still in heavy rotation a quarter-century after its release; it was receiving more than 250,000 spins per week in clubs around the world.{{sfn|Thriller 25: The Book|2008|p=26}}

sections.wikitext:
English musician [[Ian Brown]] took "Billie Jean" to number 5 on the UK charts in 2000. It was the [[A-side and B-side|B-side]] of "Dolphins Were Monkeys". Brown said, "I love Jackson. I want to do a Jackson EP with 'Thriller', 'Beat It', 'Billie Jean' and '[[Rockin' Robin (song)|Rockin' Robin]]' or 'ABC' on it. Hopefully I'll get it done". Brown later covered "Thriller" on ''Golden Gaze'', from his second solo album, ''Golden Greats''.{{sfn|Halstead|2007|pp=39–41}}<ref name="Brown">{{cite magazine|title= Brown's Thriller killer! |magazine= [[NME]] |date= March 17, 2000 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url= https://www.nme.com/news/ian-brown/2901}}</ref>

American rock musician [[Chris Cornell]] recorded "Billie Jean" for his ''[[Carry On (Chris Cornell album)|Carry On]]'' album in 2007. This version maintained the lyrics and basic melody, but radically rearranged the song with a slower acoustic interpretation influenced by country and blues. Cornell said: "I didn't plan on it. It just sort of happened organically. I changed the music quite a bit, I didn't touch the lyrics." He added, "And it's not a joke. I took a completely different approach to it, musically."<ref name="Cornell">{{cite web|first= Chris |last= Harris |title= Chris Cornell Tackles Gospel – And Michael Jackson? – On Solo LP |publisher= MTV |date= November 8, 2006 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url= http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1545231/20061108/cornell_chris.jhtml |url-status= dead |archive-date= February 1, 2009 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090201025132/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1545231/20061108/cornell_chris.jhtml}}</ref> Cornell had previously performed the song live in Europe, including an acoustic set in [[Stockholm]], [[Sweden]] in September 2006.{{sfn|Halstead|2007|pp=39–41}}<ref name="Cornell"/> He later said, "I was getting ready to do some acoustic shows on a promotional tour for ''[[Revelations (Audioslave album)|Revelations]]'' and I just wanted to have fun with it."<ref name="Cornell2">{{cite web|first= Chris |last= Harris |title= Chris Cornell Ready to Carry On as Solo Artist: 'I'm Best in My Own World' |publisher= MTV |date= April 23, 2007 |access-date= February 21, 2009 |url= http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1557741/chris-cornell-im-best-my-own-world.jhtml|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20140114095014/http://www.mtv.com/news/articles/1557741/chris-cornell-im-best-my-own-world.jhtml|url-status= dead|archive-date= January 14, 2014}}</ref> The cover received favorable reviews from critics. MTV noted the "bluesier, more pained and impassioned feel" which stripped away "any pop elements of the original".<ref name="Cornell2"/> ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' described the track as "a grim, spooky take" on Jackson's "Billie Jean", and added that it was "amusing enough, even if it sounds a lot more like [[Metallica]]'s '[[Nothing Else Matters]]'". The newspaper concluded that "Jacko's mega hit [survived] the stunt translation".<ref>{{cite news|first= Steve |last= Appleford |title= Pop Album Review – Chris Cornell |newspaper= [[Los Angeles Times]] |date= June 5, 2007 |url= http://www.calendarlive.com/music/reviews/cl-2albums05%2C0%2C6398293.story?coll=cl-albumreviews |archive-date= November 14, 2007 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20071114062427/http://www.calendarlive.com/music/reviews/cl-2albums05%2C0%2C6398293.story?coll=cl-albumreviews}}</ref> In 2008, Cornell's version was performed live by [[David Cook (singer)|David Cook]] on the [[American Idol (season 7)|seventh season]] of ''[[American Idol]]'',<ref>{{cite magazine|title= Cornell Chats 'Idol'/'Billie Jean' Performance |magazine= Billboard |access-date= August 28, 2011 |url= https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/1046017/cornell-chats-idolbillie-jean-performance}}</ref> and this version charted on ''Billboard''{{'}}s Hot 100 at No. 47.<ref>{{cite magazine|title= The Hot Spot > Who's Bad |magazine= [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |date= June 7, 2008 |volume= 120 |issue= 23 |page= 53 |issn= 0006-2510 |url= https://books.google.com/books?id=_hIEAAAAMBAJ&q=%22billie+jean%22&pg=PA53}}</ref>

In 2011, [[Fall Out Boy]] frontman [[Patrick Stump]] covered the song as part of an [[a cappella]] medley of Michael Jackson songs, in which he sang all the parts.<ref>{{cite web |first= Erica |last= Futterman |title= Patrick Stump Pays Tribute to Michael Jackson in Awesome A Cappella Medley |magazine= Rolling Stone |date= February 2, 2011 |access-date= May 10, 2011 |url= https://www.rollingstone.com/culture/blogs/rolling-stone-video-blog/patrick-stump-pays-tribute-to-michael-jackson-in-awesome-a-cappella-medley-20110202 |archive-date= May 11, 2011 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110511063216/http://www.rollingstone.com/culture/blogs/rolling-stone-video-blog/patrick-stump-pays-tribute-to-michael-jackson-in-awesome-a-cappella-medley-20110202 |url-status= dead }}</ref>

In 2015, Irish musician [[Eden (Irish musician)|EDEN]] released a remix of "Billie Jean" then separately released a cover of the song with his own vocals.<ref>{{cite web|author= Nick |title= [PREMiERE] EDEN - Billie Jean (Michael Jackson Cover) : Must Hear Cover [Free Download] |website= Thissongissick |date= November 23, 2015 |access-date= February 3, 2018 |url= http://thissongissick.com/post/premiere-eden-billie-jean-michael-jackson-cover}}</ref>

In 2022, a clip from the [[HBO]] sports documentary series ''[[Hard Knocks (documentary series)|Hard Knocks]]'' went viral, where [[Detroit Lions]] [[defensive end]] [[Aidan Hutchinson]] sang the song in front of the team as part of a [[rookie]] talent show.

A DJ named Linx created a mashup of "Billie Jean" and the 1987 Eric B. & Rakim song "I Know You Got Soul" from the original recordings, releasing it in 1997 as "Billie Jean (Got Soul)". This mashup peaked at number 34 in Sweden.

2manyDJs included a mashup of "Billie Jean", Soulwax's "Saturday" and The Residents' "Kaw-Liga" in their mix album As Heard On Radio Soulwax Pt. 2.

Scottish bhangra group Tigerstyle's song "Nachna Onda Nei" includes the backing tracks of both "Billie Jean" and "Under Pressure" by Queen and David Bowie, with new vocals by Kaka Bhaniawala. In April 2008, dance act Signature used "Nachna Onda Nei" on Britain's Got Talent in their audition and again in their final performance.
